sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details suspected unauthorized card-not-present transaction activity identified on card C00854-K2 belonging to customer C00854. On November 6, 2016 at 16:35:06, an unauthorized online transaction (ID 3435476) totaling $149.99 was processed in billing region 299 for product code R. The transaction originated from device D000255, characterized by hardware profile KFFOWI Build/LVY48F running Android 5.1.1 with Chrome Generic (screen resolution 1024x600), which was marked as newly associated with card C00854-K2. Graph analysis identified device D000255 as an active member of fraud syndicate ring 37749036, linking it to fourteen prior closed cases of confirmed fraud, including cases CC-5430, CC-4873, CC-4852, CC-4716, CC-4641, and CC-4613. During the thirty-day monitoring window between October 7, 2016, and November 9, 2016, device D000255 was also utilized across eight other compromised payment cards: C07256-K2, C06224-K2, C06299-K1, C05690-K1, C02231-K1, C08840-K1, C02716-K2, and C00941-K1. Historical analysis of the holder baseline for card C00854-K2 established no legitimate prior usage of device D000255 or recurring transaction relationship with the merchant. Furthermore, the authentic cardholder performed physical, card-present retail transactions within region 299 shortly before and after the unauthorized event, specifically transaction 3435354 ($599.92) at 15:55:26 and transaction 3435740 ($49.02) at 17:54:44. This immediate temporal and physical conflict confirms that transaction 3435476 was initiated illicitly using compromised card credentials on an unauthorized device. Total unauthorized exposure identified in this alert episode is $149.99. In response to this coordinated ring activity, the financial institution blocked card C00854-K2, placed connected cards on active monitoring, and submitted this report.

stop_reason: The investigation ended pursuant to Policy Section 6 because the fraud probability reached 0.95 (exceeding the 0.85 decisive threshold) based on two independent conclusive findings: direct attribution to a known fraud ring device (D000255) tied to 14 confirmed fraud cases, and an irreconcilable temporal contradiction with the cardholder's legitimate in-person retail activity.
